business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

Luxembourg–Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs / RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 January 2019 on the procedural organisation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, on professional obligations of financial and insurance sector actors.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport / national identity card for each shareholder, manager and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity authority of the individual's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy; if issued by a foreign notary, attach Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registrar in the corporate shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by originating state authority or consular legalization by Luxembourg diplomatic or consular office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register extract / certificate of incumbency evidencing signatory powers of the corporate shareholders and their directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or official service provider in the country of incorporation of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate board resolution authorizing incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL, designating the manager, and approving the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of each corporate shareholder / ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized board minutes followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization if originating outside Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary / incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The shareholders or their duly authorized corporate representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notary certification; if signed before a foreign notary, Hague Apostille or consular legalization is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or blocked account confirmation evidencing the availability of the minimum share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter; apostille or consular legalization is required when originating from a non-Hague state and the Luxembourg notary so demands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-know-your-client screening of all shareholders, directors, managers and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and domestic administrative records. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates. Continuous transaction monitoring is required under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) notified of all suspicious activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), accessible at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory notices and RCS entries are made in French. Latin-script names are normally accepted; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and rendered in French-readable phonetic form. A Luxembourg company name must include or be followed by the words 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' unless such indication is already clearly present.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société de gestion / Asset management company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation can be extended by written request to the LBR before expiry of the 30-day validity window, subject to issue of a new certificate of non-confusion. If the RCS/LBR rejects a name, the applicant may first request a written reasoned refusal and an internal reconsideration by the head of Luxembourg Business Registers within one month. An adverse administrative decision may then be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification; representation by a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour is required at the tribunal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where a real Luxembourg street address, lease or contractual service office, local mailing and document handling capacity, and availability of statutory records are maintained. A bare virtual mailbox without any physical service presence is not an acceptable registered office for an active online merchandising SARL.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 10-15% annual probability for a non-licensed e-commerce SARL; physical checks by tax, social security and registry authorities increase when filings are incomplete or UBO information is inconsistent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed per-shareholder and per-UBO compliance fee, market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 et seq., as modernized by the Law of 10 August 2016), read with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering (AML/UBO declarations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice, Luxembourg City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg civil-law notary, filed electronically with the RCS and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations); official RCS state fee EUR 19 (approx. USD 21), excluding notarial and bank fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 fully subscribed; cash subscriptions must be paid up to at least 20% of the subscribed capital (EUR 2,400) before signature, deposited into a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation; contributions in kind must be fully paid up; the blocked funds are released only upon issue of the RCS registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF LU_SARL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) — unanimously adopted by the sole shareholder and gérant(s) on [date]. RESOLVED: (1) the subscription of EUR 12,000 share capital, divided into 1,000 registered shares of EUR 12 each, is ratified, the paid-up portion of EUR 2,400 being blocked on the bank attestation; (2) the articles of association contained in the notarial deed of incorporation are approved; (3) the registered office is established at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (4) [name] is appointed gérant for an indefinite term with sole signature authority and instructed to complete RCS, tax and bank filings; (5) the resolution takes effect only upon RCS registration; the Company shall meanwhile act solely for incorporation purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic name-search portal (www.lbr.lu), acting through the instructed notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run the proposed corporate name 'LU_SARL' through the public RCS search to verify availability; instruct the notary to reserve the name and confirm that it is neither identical nor confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg entity and that the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' is included. Submit three ranked alternative names with the notary; the reserved name is held pending completion of the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of the intended shareholder(s) and ultimate beneficial owner(s)
Name-reservation request form signed by the founder
Three ranked alternative corporate names including the SARL suffix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for identity or confusing similarity, the notary will immediately file the next alternative name on the ranking list; a third-party opposition is cured by the objector's consent in writing or by selecting a non-conflicting reserved name.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises for customs and EORI matters; all official declarations are filed electronically through the MyGuichet.lu portal and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign founders incorporate the SARL by notarized deed and register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) to obtain the institutional matricule number, which functions as the definitive corporate TIN; thereafter the SARL applies to the AEDT for a VAT identification number in the format LU plus 8 digits (resident registration for the Luxembourg SARL, or non-established taxable person procedure via form 1020 for foreign PEs); a separate EORI number is requested from the customs administration to enable import and export declarations. Registration is performed electronically with authenticated eIDs, and non-established taxpayers may appoint a fiscal representative for VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A resident SARL is a capital-company taxpayer subject to corporate income tax (CIT 17%), the solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT), and municipal business tax (aggregate statutory burden in Luxembourg City approx. 24.94%); worldwide income is taxable on residence; non-residents are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a permanent establishment; no pass-through eligibility applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime. Available elections include the opt-in fiscal unity (integration fiscale) for 95%-or-more owned resident group companies upon joint application, the VAT grouping (assujetti unique) election, the deemed-resident election for qualifying commercial permanent establishments, and the election to conclude arm's-length advance pricing agreements. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 1 and 2 operate mandatorily and are not elective; the participation exemption is applied automatically upon satisfaction of holding period, shareholding and substance conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee / TVA) implemented pursuant to EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (VAT-exclusive) for the domestic small-business exemption; EUR 10,000 annual intra-Community distance-sales threshold for jewelry, watches and fashion goods; no registration threshold applies to non-established suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg; registration becomes mandatory immediately on breach of the de minimis threshold or upon taxable importation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general B2B e-invoicing mandate and no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Luxembourg; PEPPOL/EN 16931 e-invoicing is mandatory for B2G invoices to the Luxembourg State under Directive 2014/55/EU transposition; VAT returns and recapitulative statements are e-filed via MyGuichet.lu; taxpayers must retain SAF-T-type digital audit files and complete audit trails for AEDT inspection; Luxembourg is monitoring the EU ViDA e-invoicing and reporting proposals.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT applies to (i) export supplies of jewelry, watches and fashion goods dispatched or transported outside the EU, provided tangible proof of export is retained in conformity with Article 146 of the VAT Directive and Luxembourg national rules; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to purchasers holding a valid EU VAT identification number, subject to EC Sales List reporting; and (iii) ancillary freight, transport and handling services directly linked to exported goods. The exporter must substantiate physical movement out of the EU, the sale consideration, customer identity and the settlement rails used.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration lodged through the EU Customs Declaration System (CDS) via the Single Administrative Document (SAD) or accepted postal/courier outward manifests
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or final-mile courier delivery proof evidencing departure of the goods from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice with Incoterms 2020, 8-digit HS classification (jewelry 7113/7117; watches 9101/9102/9105) and full sale consideration
For intra-Community zero-rating: customer VAT registration certificate and VIES validation report
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 settlement advice, or payment acquirer (Stripe/PayPal) settlement statements proving remittance of export proceeds
EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) and, where applicable, Intrastat dispatch declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating is prosecuted as VAT fraud: the AEDT and the customs administration jointly audit export transactions using digital platform data, courier manifests, HS-code profiling and payment rail analytics. Remedial measures include retrospective VAT reassessment and clawback of improperly zero-rated output tax, default interest at 0.6% per month, administrative penalties up to 100% of the evaded VAT, and, under the criminal tax procedure law of 17 March 2020, fines ranging from EUR 125,000 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 5 to 10 years for aggravated tax fraud; the VAT assessment limitation period is extended to 10 years upon proof of fraud or wilful misconduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) for central banking and monetary policy coordination with the European Central Bank; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) regulates banking conduct and foreign exchange intermediation. Luxembourg has no separate foreign exchange administration; transactions are governed by EU capital movement freedoms under Articles 63–66 TFEU and the Luxembourg Monetary Law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. No exchange controls or approval requirements exist for profit remittances, dividend distributions, or repatriation of capital. A Luxembourg SARL may freely open foreign currency accounts and settle in any convertible currency, subject only to general EU sanctions and anti-money laundering rules. The sole legal restriction is the balance-sheet maintenance of subscribed minimum capital (EUR 12,000 for SARL) under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender, repurchase, or mandatory conversion obligation exists in Luxembourg. Export receipts may be held indefinitely in EUR or in foreign currency at the exporter's discretion. Corporate treasury should nevertheless document all export sales and payment inflows in the statutory annual accounts for taxable income determination.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passported into Luxembourg, such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, or Adyen, for operating the daily e-commerce clearing and marketpay placeouts to customers. These EMIs provide easier API integration for Stripe/PayPal settlement and international payout. However, they cannot be used for the statutory statutory capital escrow account required for a Luxembourg SARL, and CSSF supervision requires that client funds be safeguarded in segregated accounts at a credit institution. The e-commerce business model (jewelry/watches) is treated as medium-high money laundering risk, so EMIs will apply additional KYC scrutiny and transaction monitoring.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear physically if the bank offers a fully remote onboarding process using LuxTrust authentication for electronic signatures. In practice, most Tier 1 Luxembourg banks require a physical meeting or a video KYC session with original certificated documents for non-resident directors and for high AML-risk sectors. For non-EU directors, a face-to-face interview at the bank's registered office in Luxembourg is generally mandated. Remote opening with a documentary apostille is possible but will result in extended onboarding timelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO jurisdiction combined with opaque beneficial ownership in non-OECD tax havens or sanctioned territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified registry extracts from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), a signed beneficial ownership declaration under the Luxembourg UBO Register Act of 13 January 2019, notarial certificate of the SARL's incorporation, bank references from the UBOs, written source-of-wealth analysis with bank statements for the previous 12 months, and a copy of the shareholder register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity and digital marketplace exposure for high-value watches and jewelry, presenting unexplained international payment flows from multiple e-commerce gateways.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan mapping the ISIC 4791 model, contractual settlement structure and fee statements from Stripe/PayPal, description of goods and sourcing invoices, complete customer and supplier due diligence files, chargeback and refund analytics, transaction flow charts, and a mandatory AML/CTF programme with an appointed compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Artefact and precious goods provenance risk: jewelry/watch inventory sourced from outside the EU that may involve antique/cultural property or diamond-related sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificates of authenticity, supplier certificates of provenance, EU market surveillance and nominal hallmarking documentation for precious metals, Kimberley Process Certificate if rough diamonds are involved, customs declarations (EU Single Administrative Document), import duty records, and a product due diligence policy aligned with the EU Conflict Minerals Regulation (EU 2017/821).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inject equity contributions via SEPA credit transfer or SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's segregated capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution. Use EBICS purpose code 'CAPIT' (from the EBA EPC list) and include in the remittance field the share subscription certificate number and the RCS registration number. For second and subsequent tranches, reference the notarised capital increase deed and the board resolution authorising the injection. The bank may request a notarial certificate of deposit for the blocked account and UBO confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of supplier invoices for jewellery and timepieces should be executed through SWIFT MT103 (single payment), SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR-denominated intra-EEA), or a commercial letter of credit (open at the Luxembourg relationship bank) for high-value import contracts. Remittance advice must encode the invoice number, purchase order, and HS code. If the goods include rough diamonds or controlled items, the clearing rail must include the Kimberley Process Certificate and EU customs release declaration. For recurring payouts to third-party logistics providers, use API-driven International ACH/SWIFT payment protocols through the bank's corporate internet portal.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forward contracts (up to 24 months) with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution for EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP, EUR/INR, and EUR/CNY exposures.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies subject to onshore restrictions (e.g., INR, CNY offshore in HKD) with offshore settlement in a convertible currency.
Cross-currency swaps on EUR/USD to hedge long-term USD-denominated vendor payment obligations.

FX currency options on major pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) solely for transactional hedging, not for speculative purposes, and always documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or local collapsed master agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filing of the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year SARL by 31 July, provided the shareholders approve the annual accounts within 6 months and the filing is completed within 1 month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fines on directors/managers typically EUR 500–EUR 10,000; repeated non-filing permits the Commercial Court, upon motion by the Public Prosecutor, to order dissolution of the company; tax authorities may impose separate penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (confirmative annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: UBO Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 15 March of each calendar year, confirming the UBO data as at 31 December; a separate UBO update is due within 1 month of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 15,000 for failure to file or confirm UBO information; intentional false declarations may trigger criminal penalties; after formal reminder, the entity may be struck off or suspended from the RCS, causing loss of legal standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint an accredited statutory auditor if it exceeds at least two of the following criteria at the balance-sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50. For the first financial year, the criteria are assessed as at the close of that year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2008 for SARL annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is optional for consolidated financial statements and mandatory for listed entities; e-commerce jewellery and luxury watch activities are recorded under customary LGAAP inventory and revenue recognition rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every year the SARL must electronically reconfirm the complete UBO file by 15 March. The confirmation must verify the identity, nationality, address and ownership percentage of each beneficial owner as at 31 December. After confirmation, any subsequent share transfer or UBO change requires an updated declaration filed within one month and an entry in the Register of Members before the transfer can be asserted against third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and management decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $9,000 – $22,000 per annual statutory audit engagement, if mandatory or prudently procured
